dedupe_keys.name: ipacs model improving the flow of patients between acute community and social care discharge to assess simulation

description: This model helps an English health and care system decide how much community capacity it needs so that patients ready to leave hospital are not stuck waiting for home care, a community bed or a care home place. The producers are the IPACS project team, funded by Health Data Research UK from 2020 to 2023: Alison Harper and Martin Pitt of the University of Exeter, Zehra Onen Dumlu and Christos Vasilakis of the University of Bath, and Richard Wood and Paul Forte of the NHS integrated care board for Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire. It is a stochastic discrete-event simulation of the discharge-to-assess pathways: users enter arrival rates, lengths of stay and capacities in an Excel file, and the model estimates occupancy, the number of patients with a delayed discharge, days spent waiting and total cost over time. Coverage is the Bristol area system where it was built, but any system can supply its own parameters. The code and documentation are available free on GitHub and Zenodo under the GNU General Public License, with the data behind a companion paper on visits-based home care. Caveats: parameters must be estimated locally, the project ended in 2023 with the last code change in May 2023, and the documentation is in PDF guides in the repository. Simulation uses: sizing community and social care capacity to relieve hospital bed pressure in winter or surges. Related records: patientflow (model-patientflow) and the NHP demand model (model-nhp-demand-model) cover hospital demand.
